newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended slightly firm after retracing early losses sparked by some profit-taking but Amplat's move to merge its operations stole the limelight.
Amplat's Lebowa Platinum Ltd finished up 110 cents at 440 cents following Amplats' announcement on Tuesday that all its operation would now be put in Rusplats.
Amplats was last up 95 cents to a new year high of 34.95 rand while Rustenberg failed to take note of the jovial mood in the Amplats stable, ending down 50 cents at 76.00 rand.
"I will say the main feature today has been the platinum side of the market. Guys definately see this Amplat's restructuring as positive news," one dealer said.

The market which failed to take a cue from Wall Street's climb overnight was also buoyed by U.S. agency Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co's move to assign an investment grade BBB minus rating to the country's foreign currency obligations.

"We've had a bit of positive news on the market today with the Duff & Phelps rating coming through. People are now expecting a good S & P (Standard & Poor's) rating to come through as well," another dealer said.
The industrial index ended up 3.3 points to 8,504.7, the gold index was down 12.8 points to 1,164.5 and the all-share index gained 20.6 points to 7,286.1.

Comments by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel that an interest rate cut was likely later this year had helped the market's financial index to close at another fresh high, although the rate cut news were now old news, dealers said.
The financial index ended up 45.5 points to 9,739.9.
Worries about the rand's recent slide on jitters about foreign exchange control relaxations were starting to dissipate.
The rand fell to 4.50 bid on the dollar on Monday -- its lowest level in four months -- but has since come back to hold steady around 4.49 bid.
"The rand has looked a bit stronger...which is more positive for the market," one said.
Volumes on the day were high with 837 million rand worth of shares traded.

Big volumes were seen in iron and steel stock Iscor which traded 3.4 million shares worth around 10.9 million rand and life firm Metlife which saw over four million shares change hands worth 36.4 million rand.
Dealers said gold shares were disappointing on the day as bullion remained dull, hovering in its recent $343-$344 range.
On the gold board Vaal ended down 75 cents at 270.00 rand while Kloof shed 70 cents to 28.50 rand and Goldfields dumped 150 cents to 110.00 rand.
Dealers expected the overall market to hold around current levels on Thursday with the eyes focused on Wall Street's start by the local close.

"People are looking up on Wall Street although we have not really followed it closely," said Johan Marais, a director at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollak, adding that the market appeared to be swayed somewhat by futures players ahead of the close-out of June contracts next week.
In the broader market advancers just led decliners 187 to 182 and there were 29 news highs and 20 new lows.
Dealers said the share futures, which had started weaker on rand concerns, had held a touch weaker amid some reluctance by players to take positions ahead of the close-out.
"The futures market has been exceptionally thin today," one futures trader said.
The all-share June contract was last at 6,554/59 from 6,559 settlement, the industrial June contract at 8,160/70 from 8,170 settlement and the June gold contract at 808/16 from 826.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
